summary: Configured zram-generator on node1 to provide 981 MB of zstd-compressed in-memory swap (exceeds the 512 MB minimum), with swap-priority 100 so it is preferred over any disk-backed swap (none present). The unit is generator-based (dev-zram0.swap / systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service, "static", regenerated by systemd at every boot from /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf), so it activates automatically at boot with no manual enable step. Verified across a full reboot of node1: boot ID changed from d6298ced-a924-4ce7-bbed-0fb8179eda8e to 1c856cb8-f1f8-45eb-bfc9-e215f6fc9369 (uptime reset to 0), and post-reboot swapon/zramctl show the same 981M zstd zram0 swap active with priority 100 automatically, with no other swap devices competing.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 baseline: AlmaLinux 9.6, no existing swap, zram module not loaded
Installed zram-generator package via dnf (AppStream repo)
Wrote /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf with zram0 sized max(ram/2, 512) MB, zstd compression, swap-priority=100, fs-type=swap
Reloaded systemd and started systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service, verified 981M zstd zram swap active with priority 100 and no competing disk swap
Confirmed dev-zram0.swap and systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service are generator-created (static) units requiring no manual enable, ensuring boot persistence
Captured baseline boot_id and uptime, then issued a background-delayed systemctl reboot so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, confirming boot_id changed and uptime reset (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce)
Re-verified post-reboot that the 981M zstd zram swap is active automatically with priority 100, matching pre-reboot state

evidence.requirement: At least 512 MB compressed in-memory swap active on node1
evidence.summary: After creating zram0 via zram-generator, swapon --show and zramctl show /dev/zram0, 981M, algorithm zstd, active as [SWAP]
zram0 configured with swap-priority=100; baseline showed zero pre-existing disk swap devices (empty /proc/swaps), so zram is the only and highest-priority swap

dev-zram0.swap and systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service are systemd-generator-created static units (regenerated from /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf on every boot); post-reboot check confirms both are active without any manual step
Captured boot_id d6298ced-a924-4ce7-bbed-0fb8179eda8e, uptime, and confirmed zram swap active and services active pre-restart
Backgrounded systemctl reboot with a 2s delay so the exec call returning 'reboot scheduled, pid 8907' completed before the node went down

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity (actual restart, not just service bounce)
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id read as 1c856cb8-f1f8-45eb-bfc9-e215f6fc9369 (differs from baseline d6298ced...) and uptime shows 0 minutes, proving a genuine reboot

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required service/data (zram swap)
evidence.summary: After reboot, swapon --show and zramctl again show 981M zstd zram0 swap active with priority 100, matching pre-restart state, with dev-zram0.swap and systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service both active
